title: Håstad's switching lemma for bounded-width DNFs
statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, and let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables whose width is at most $w$, so that every term of $f$ has at most $w$ literals. Suppose that $5s \le n$, that no term of $f$ contains two distinct literals on the same variable, and that no term of $f$ repeats a literal. Call a restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables an $s$-restriction if it leaves exactly $s$ variables free, and call it bad (at depth $d$) if the restricted function $f|_\rho$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$. Then the number $N$ of $s$-restrictions that are bad satisfies
\[
  N \cdot n^{d} \;\le\; \binom{n}{s}\, 2^{\,n-s}\, (10\,s\,w)^{d}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: within each term, two literals on the same variable are identical
each term has no repeated literal
count restricts to restrictions with exactly s free variables (s-restrictions)
bad means restricted function has decision-tree depth > d
replaced:
Let $n>0$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a DNF formula, and fix $w,s,d\in\bbn$.
Assume
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\text{width}(f)\le w$ (width counted as list length, see
        Section~\ref{sec:faithfulness}),
  \item $5s \le n$,
  \item $f$ satisfies the \emph{non-contradictory clause} hypothesis
        \texttt{hnd}: for every term $t\in f$ and every pair of literals
        $\ell_1,\ell_2\in t$, if $\ell_1.\mathrm{var}=\ell_2.\mathrm{var}$ then
        $\ell_1=\ell_2$.
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
  \bigl|\{\,\rho : \rho\text{ is an $s$-restriction and }
        \mathrm{dtDepth}(f|_\rho)>d\,\}\bigr| \cdot n^d
  \;\le\;
  \mathrm{numSRestrictions}(n,s)\,\cdot\,(10\,s\,w)^d.
\]
